note: Ratchet for `scripts/reference-check.py` — the Rust and TypeScript half of the question `./gradlew :peer:structureReport` has been asking of Java. `entries` are exported symbols that nothing outside their own file names, each with the reason it is still here; `limit` caps that list and it may only go DOWN. `test_only_limit` and `local_only_limit` are the other two counters: a symbol only a test names, and a symbol only its own file names. Those are budgets rather than lists for the same reason `budget.json` counts `test_only_methods` instead of enumerating them — the population is large and what matters is that it falls.
measured: 2026-08-09 on fix/pr222-tooling-ref, by running `scripts/reference-check.py --json` on this tree and reading `symbols_inspected` and `files_searched` out of the document it prints: 2,246 exported symbols across 1,715 searched files, with a further 62 not asked because their name is in `UNIVERSAL` and 3 not asked because they are `#[no_mangle]` ABI entry points. Read the numbers off a run; do not carry them forward. The figure this field used to give, '989 exported symbols in 1,735 searched files', was the third wrong file count in its own lineage — the tool printed 1,715 on every run of that same code, and the stamp before it (1,017 symbols, 1,734 files) belonged to a run taken while the allowlist was still inside the reference index, so writing an entry here gave its symbol a test reference and moved it out of `unreferenced`. 989 was a true symbol count for a walker that latched on the first `#[cfg(test)]` and never reset, which excused 28 production `pub fn` from the question, and for an extractor that asked about `pub fn` and nothing else — no `pub struct`, `const`, `enum`, `trait`, `type`, `static`, no `pub` field, and no `export default function`. Both are fixed, which is why the population trebled. THE THREE LIMITS BELOW ARE NOT RE-STAMPED HERE: they are ratchet values and a ratchet re-measured on one branch of a parallel wave loosens silently on merge, so the integrator re-measures once on the combined tree. Against this tree the required values are `limit` 18 (unchanged; all 18 entries still flag, none is stale), `test_only_limit` 12 (unchanged, exactly on its limit) and `local_only_limit` 153, up from 90 — 62 of the 63 newly-visible exported-but-local symbols are the shapes the extractor could not see before, and the 63rd is `rendezvous/src/service.rs:183 note_nat`, which the `#[cfg(test)]` latch was hiding. No new entry is needed in the list below: the extension added zero unreferenced symbols. Every one of the 18 entries was hand-verified by grepping the whole tree for its name: zero false positives. They are a work item, not a debt to be renewed.
